name: CRM
description: Contacts, companies/accounts, leads, deals/opportunities and pipelines, activities/tasks, email/calendar sync, quotes, segmentation, and forecasting for a B2B sales team.

sources.title: NextCRM
sources.notes: Verified full LICENSE file: plain MIT, no exceptions. Rich Prisma schema (~90 models). Confirmed models: crm_Contacts, crm_Accounts (with member_of parent-account field), crm_Leads (lead_source/status/type lookups, assigned_accounts FK, no explicit convert action found), crm_Opportunities + crm_Opportunities_Sales_Stages + crm_OpportunityLineItems + approval_status workflow (quote/SOW approval before sending), crm_FunnelSettings (kill/recycle/cadence-touch follow-up timers), crm_Activities + Tasks (polymorphic activity links), crm_Products/crm_ProductCategories/crm_AccountProducts, crm_Targets/crm_TargetLists (segmentation, tags, do-not-email), crm_campaigns, crm_Report_Config/crm_Report_Schedule, EmailAccount/Email (IMAP/SMTP sync), CalendarConnection/crm_CalendarEvents (Google OAuth). Confirmed CSV import for products (actions/crm/products/import-products.ts) and targets (actions/crm/targets/import-targets.ts), not contacts specifically. Copy-safe.

sources.title: EspoCRM
sources.notes: AGPL-3.0, reference-only. Read over the GitHub API: `application/Espo/Modules/Crm/Resources/metadata/entityDefs/Lead.json` — `status` options are exactly ['New','Assigned','In Process','Converted','Recycled','Dead'], plus `convertedAt` and `createdAccount`/`createdContact`/`createdOpportunity` links, which is direct evidence for the lead state machine and for conversion producing three records; `Opportunity.json` — `stage` options ['Prospecting','Qualification','Proposal','Negotiation','Closed Won','Closed Lost']; `assignedUser` field. Notably its core has NO Quote, Product, Report or Workflow entityDef (those are the paid Advanced Pack), so Espo is deliberately NOT cited for those features.

sources.title: Odoo CRM (addons/crm)
sources.license: LGPL-3.0 (per addon manifest; Odoo licenses per-addon, not repo-wide)
sources.notes: LGPL-3.0 per addon manifest, reference-only. Read over the GitHub API at branch 18.0: `addons/crm/models/crm_lead.py` (`type` lead/opportunity selection, `date_conversion`, `stage_id`, `user_id`, `team_id`, `probability`, `lost_reason_id`), `addons/crm/models/` listing (`crm_team.py`, `crm_team_member.py`, `crm_lead_scoring_frequency.py`, `crm_stage.py`), `odoo/addons/base/models/res_partner.py` (`parent_id` 'Related Company' + `child_ids` + `commercial_partner_id` — the account hierarchy), and the presence of the `sale` (with `sale_order.py`/`sale_order_line.py`), `base_automation`, `base_import`, `board`, `spreadsheet_dashboard`, `google_calendar`, `microsoft_calendar` and `mass_mailing` addons.

sources.title: SuiteCRM
sources.notes: AGPL-3.0, reference-only: read for its data model, never copied. `salesagility/SuiteCRM` redirects to `SuiteCRM/SuiteCRM`. Read over the GitHub API (not cloned): `modules/` listing, `modules/Accounts/vardefs.php` (`parent_id` + `member_of` account hierarchy), `modules/Leads/vardefs.php` (`converted` flag, comment 'Has Lead been converted to a Contact'), `include/SugarObjects/implements/assignable/vardefs.php` (`assigned_user_id` on every assignable module). The AOS_* modules (Quotes, Products, Products_Quotes, Line_Item_Groups, Invoices, Contracts, PDF_Templates), AOR_* reporting modules, and AOW_* workflow modules are in core, which is what makes quotes, line items, reporting and automation corroborated rather than assumed.

sources.title: Twenty
sources.license: Mixed: AGPL-3.0 with an "Application Exception" for APIs/webhooks/manifests, plus separately MIT-licensed SDK/UI packages, plus commercially-licensed enterprise files
sources.notes: License is NOASSERTION on GitHub (AGPL-3.0 with an enterprise carve-out) — reference-only, and verify the carve-out before any reuse. Read over the GitHub API: `packages/twenty-server/src/modules/{person,company,opportunity,note,task}/standard-objects/*.workspace-entity.ts` — a modern CRM that still ships exactly person, company, opportunity, note and task as standard objects, with `note-target`/`task-target` join entities behind the activity timeline. Cited as a third corroboration of the core object set only.

features.name: Contacts
features.description: Individual people records with contact details, linked to companies, deals, and activities.

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations confirm a dedicated contact entity distinct from company/account.

features.name: Companies / accounts
features.description: Organization records that group contacts and deals, with optional parent/subsidiary hierarchy.

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations. nextcrm's crm_Accounts.member_of field additionally confirms parent-account hierarchy.

features.name: Leads
features.description: Unqualified prospects captured before they become a contact/account and a deal.

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations, each with lead source/status/type lookups.

features.name: Lead conversion
features.description: Convert a qualified lead into a contact, account, and an opportunity, preserving lineage back to the original lead.

provenance.notes: Verified in three independent implementations: EspoCRM Lead.status includes 'Converted' with convertedAt and createdAccount/createdContact/createdOpportunity links; SuiteCRM Leads.vardefs has a `converted` flag documented as 'Has Lead been converted to a Contact (and other Sugar objects)'; Odoo crm.lead carries a lead/opportunity `type` plus `date_conversion`. The three-record outcome (account + contact + opportunity) is Espo's explicit model.

features.name: Deals / opportunities and pipelines
features.description: Sales opportunities moving through one or more configurable pipelines and stages, with value and close date.

provenance.notes: Stage vocabularies were read directly: EspoCRM Opportunity.stage is ['Prospecting','Qualification','Proposal','Negotiation','Closed Won','Closed Lost']; Odoo separates stage_id (crm.stage) from probability and lost_reason_id. Twenty ships opportunity as a standard object.

features.name: Activities and tasks
features.description: Calls, meetings, notes, and follow-up tasks logged against a contact, company, lead, or deal.

provenance.notes: Corroborated across four: SuiteCRM Calls/Meetings/Tasks modules, Odoo mail_activity, Twenty's task and note standard objects with task-target/note-target join entities, plus EspoCRM and nextcrm.

features.name: Unified contact timeline
features.description: A single chronological view of every activity, email, and document tied to a contact, company, or deal.

provenance.notes: Twenty's `note-target` and `task-target` join entities are the clearest evidence that the timeline is a polymorphic association rather than a log table; SuiteCRM's activity panels and EspoCRM's stream corroborate.

features.name: Record assignment
features.description: Assign a lead, deal, or account to a specific sales rep.

provenance.notes: Verified in three independent implementations: SuiteCRM puts `assigned_user_id` in the shared assignable SugarObjects template so every module has it; EspoCRM has `assignedUser` on Lead; Odoo crm.lead has both `user_id` and `team_id`, with `crm_team_member.py` for team-level assignment. Team/round-robin routing is Odoo-specific and is the weaker half of this claim.

features.name: Email sync
features.description: Two-way email sync (IMAP/SMTP or provider OAuth) that logs sent/received email against the matching contact or deal.

provenance.notes: nextcrm: EmailAccount/Email models with IMAP/SMTP UID sync state. EspoCRM: EmailAccount/InboundEmail in its core entityDefs list. Two independent sources.

features.name: Calendar sync
features.description: Sync meetings scheduled in the CRM with an external calendar (Google/Outlook) and vice versa.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations verified: SuiteCRM has Calendar and CalendarAccount modules; Odoo ships separate `google_calendar` and `microsoft_calendar` addons alongside `calendar`. Two provider-specific addons rather than one standard is itself the finding — CalDAV/iCalendar is the protocol, but bidirectional sync is per-provider in practice.

features.name: Campaign management
features.description: Group leads and deals under a marketing campaign to track source and attribution.

provenance.notes: nextcrm: crm_campaigns linked from both Leads and Opportunities. EspoCRM: Campaign is one of its confirmed core entities. Two independent sources.

features.name: Segmentation
features.description: Dynamic lists of contacts/leads built from filter criteria, used for targeted outreach.

provenance.notes: nextcrm: crm_Targets/crm_TargetLists (tags, do-not-email, conversion tracking, CSV import). EspoCRM: TargetList tied to Campaign. Two independent sources.

features.name: Quotes
features.description: A priced proposal generated from a deal's line items, routed for internal approval before it is sent to the customer.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations verified: SuiteCRM ships AOS_Quotes (with AOS_PDF_Templates) in core; Odoo models this as sale.order in the `sale` addon. EspoCRM core has no Quote entity — quotes are in its paid Advanced Pack — so this is not universal, hence `recommended`.

features.name: Deal line items / product catalog
features.description: A product/price catalog that can be attached as line items to a deal or quote.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations verified: SuiteCRM has AOS_Products, AOS_Products_Quotes and AOS_Line_Item_Groups; Odoo has sale_order_line.py plus product_template/product_product. Line-item grouping is SuiteCRM-specific detail, not a general expectation.

features.name: Pipeline automation
features.description: Rule-based automation on deal/lead lifecycle events: stage-change timers, kill/recycle rules, scheduled follow-up cadences.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations verified: SuiteCRM ships AOW_WorkFlow with AOW_Conditions and AOW_Actions in core; Odoo provides the generic `base_automation` addon and, for scoring, `crm_lead_scoring_frequency.py`. EspoCRM's equivalent is paid, so automation is `recommended`, not expected.

features.name: Sales forecasting
features.description: Pipeline-based revenue forecast, weighted by stage probability, often with recurring-revenue (MRR) tracking.

provenance.notes: Odoo: probability/automated_probability, recurring_revenue/MRR fields, dedicated forecast_graph/forecast_pivot views — the strongest evidence found. nextcrm: crm_Report_Config/crm_Report_Schedule with a 'sales' report category is weaker, indirect evidence. EspoCRM's core lacks a forecasting entity. Two sources, one strong one weak — recommended, not core.

features.name: Account hierarchy
features.description: Parent/subsidiary relationships between company accounts, with rollup reporting.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations verified: SuiteCRM Accounts has `parent_id` plus a `member_of` link; Odoo res.partner has `parent_id` ('Related Company'), `child_ids` and a derived `commercial_partner_id`. EspoCRM core has no account parent link at all, which is why this stays `medium` and `optional` rather than common.

features.name: Sales reports and dashboards
features.description: Pipeline, activity, and win/loss reporting dashboards for sales management.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations verified: SuiteCRM ships AOR_Reports, AOR_Charts and AOR_Scheduled_Reports in core; Odoo provides the `board` and `spreadsheet_dashboard` addons. Overlaps `shared.reporting` — this feature is the CRM-specific report set (pipeline, forecast, activity), not a reporting engine.

features.name: Bulk data import
features.description: CSV import of segments/target lists and products, with a review step before committing records.

provenance.notes: Verified in three independent implementations: SuiteCRM has an `Import` module, EspoCRM an `Import` entityDef in its core (not the paid pack), Odoo the `base_import` addon. Overlaps `shared.import_export`; kept here because CRM import carries domain-specific duplicate handling.

features.name: Duplicate Detection and Merge
features.description: Surface probable duplicate leads, contacts, or accounts and merge them into one surviving record, carrying related activity across.
ai_opportunities: ranking probable duplicates for a human to confirm
suggesting which field value survives a merge

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations verified: Odoo crm.lead computes `duplicate_lead_ids` via `_compute_potential_lead_duplicates` (matching on the company email domain among other rules); SuiteCRM ships a `MergeRecords` module. Matching heuristics differ per product, so only the existence of the capability is corroborated, not any particular algorithm.

features.name: Consent and Marketing Preferences
features.description: Record the lawful basis or consent behind holding a contact, and their opt-in/opt-out state per channel, so outbound sending can be suppressed at source.

provenance.notes: Authoritative: GDPR Art. 6 (lawful basis) and Art. 21 (right to object) require the basis and the objection to be recorded and honoured; CAN-SPAM requires a working opt-out honoured within ten business days. EspoCRM's TargetList carries opt-out state, corroborating that suppression is modelled at the recipient rather than per send.
